newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy machine tool orders fell 29 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Italy machine tool orders fell 29 pct in 1996.

text.p: Italian machine tool orders fell 27.8 percent in 1996 due to a decline in demand at home and abroad, the machine tool producers' association UCIMU said.
It said in a statement that domestic demand dropped 35.7 percent while foreign orders were 19.1 percent down.
Data for the last quarter of 1996 confirmed a continuing contraction in demand, down 25.6 percent at home and 17.9 percent abroad.

UCIMU said Italy had the worst year among major machine tool manufacturing countries. It said Germany saw a fall in orders of just eight percent in the first 10 months of 1996, while demand in the United States was steady at current high levels.
In 1997, UCIMU said it forecast a recovery in China's market after a pause marking the end of the previous five-year plan.
